cover letter
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline required.

Minimum of five years of specialized accounting experience, preferably within intellectual property, research administration, grants, or legal finance, higher education, or a comparable complex financial environment.
Advance experience using financial transactions and systems, as well as related policy, accounting, and unique regulatory compliance requirements.

The Senior IP Accountant serves as a key senior-level financial resource within Innovation Transfer and Entrepreneurship (ITE), supporting the University of California's systemwide intellectual property and technology transfer operations. This role manages a portfolio of 300+ active licenses and provides financial stewardship by overseeing the full lifecycle of intellectual property assets across 10 UC locations. This position provides financial stewardship from agreement setup through revenue collection, patent cost recovery, compliance monitoring, and inventor distributions in alignment with UC policies, contractual obligations, and systemwide business practices. This position applies sound financial judgment, leverages strong contract interpretation skills, and makes sure non-financial and financial terms are accurately reflected in the intellectual property management system; supports UC locations and works with internal stakeholders, licensees, and external service providers to ensure accurate, compliant, transparent, and timely financial administration to resolve financial issues.

50% Revenue & Royalty Management. Contract Review: Review license agreements to identify, interpret, and operationalize key financial obligations consistent with UC policy, systemwide practices, and agreement-specific obligations, including tiered royalties, sublicensing revenue shares, and milestone payments. Invoicing: Set up and maintain Agreement Financial Terms (AFT) in Wellspring Evolve to support accurate, timely, auditable, and systemwide-consistent billing processes. Royalty Report Review: Evaluate licensee royalty reports for accuracy and confirm that Net Sales definitions and related financial terms are applied in accordance with applicable agreements, UC requirements, and established business processes according to each agreement.
This is a fully remote position within California.

20% Patent Cost Recovery & Expense Oversight. Legal Invoice Review: Partner with Patent Prosecution and UC location stakeholders to review outside counsel invoices and ensure patent-related costs are accurately allocated to the appropriate intellectual property/ assets. Licensee Reimbursement: Identify reimbursable patent prosecution expenses and administer timely invoicing to support institutional cost recovery and alignment with UC financial stewardship expectations. Internal Chargebacks: Maintain the internal debt ledger and coordinate chargebacks to originating UC locations or units for patent costs associated with unlicensed technologies.

20% Compliance & Reporting: Prepare and distribute monthly financial health dashboards for the 10 UC locations, comparing patient-related expenses against generated revenue to support transparency, informed decision-making, and systemwide financial oversight.

10% Strategic Collections & Dispute Resolution. Provide accounting analysis and financial evidence for licensing disputes, infringement claims, and contract disagreements; quantify damages, unpaid royalties, interest calculations, and financial exposure; support negotiations with financial models, settlement scenarios, and documentation.
Advanced proficiency with Wellspring Evolve and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, including such as Oracle, UCPath, or comparable financial platforms.
Understanding of the interrelationship between procedures and desired results.
Ability to interpret complex legal agreements and translate contractual, UC policy, and business requirements obligations into accurate, compliant financial processes.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with UC locations, corporate partners, faculty inventors, campus stakeholders, and internal leadership.
Advanced knowledge of accounting function.
Ability to extract, verify, and compile accounting information from multiple sources to complete work assignments.
Advanced ability to effectively present complex accounting and finance related information verbally and in writing.
Advanced knowledge of common desktop / web applications.
Advanced knowledge of analytical procedures used in accounting project of complex scope.
